core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Firnas corresponds to the Arabic form فِرناس (Arabic فرناس (Firnās) — a personal name, not a common noun). Its core sense is paradise flyer. Firnas (فِرناس) is an Arabic personal name, best known from the Andalusi polymath ʿAbbās ibn Firnās (c. 809–887 CE), a pioneer of early gliding. The word itself has no established dictionary meaning; the 'paradise flyer' gloss in the source is a modern association with Ibn Firnas's flight experiments, not a lexical meaning, and is marked accordingly. A crater on the Moon is named after Ibn Firnas.
